title: Assemble/verify policy hash mismatch breaks end-to-end round-trip
description:
## Goal
Make `airlock assemble` and `airlock verify` agree on policy hash semantics so a provenance file emitted by `assemble` is accepted by `verify`.

## Reproduction
1. Run `airlock assemble` with any valid policy/input/system prompt.
2. Wrap the emitted prompt into a valid request payload.
3. Run `airlock verify` with the same policy, prompt, and emitted provenance.
4. Current result: exit 2 with `E_BAD_PROVENANCE` because `prompt_provenance.policy_hash` differs from `verify`'s expected policy hash.

## Observed
- `src/commands/assemble.rs` writes `prompt_provenance.policy_hash` from `policy::hash_policy(path)`, which hashes raw YAML bytes.
- `src/commands/verify.rs` compares against `canonical_policy_hash(&policy)`, which hashes canonicalized policy content.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A provenance file emitted by `airlock assemble` is accepted by `airlock verify` when all other inputs match.
- Policy hash semantics are consistent across command and library surfaces.
- Add regression coverage for assemble -> verify round-trip.
close_reason: completed

title: Phase A: RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON with cross-implementation test
description:
Parent al-39t. Depends on al-1ay (land binding first, then swap the canonicalizer once).

WHY: third parties must be able to recompute prompt_payload_hash and request_payload_hash with a standard library. The in-house canonical_json_bytes is airlock-specific; RFC 8785 is the interoperable choice (sorted keys, specific number formatting, UTF-16 code unit ordering).

TESTS: RFC 8785 vectors; number edge cases (1.0 vs 1, -0, large ints); non-ASCII key ordering; hash stability golden files.

title: SEC archive regex is over-escaped in baseline/sample policies
description:
## Goal
Correct over-escaped `sec.gov/Archives` forbidden-pattern rules in baseline/sample policies so SEC archive URLs are actually detected during boundary scanning.

## Observed
- The current policy text uses `sec\.gov/Archives` in YAML plain scalars.
- YAML preserves both backslashes, so the compiled regex looks for a literal backslash before the dot and does not match `https://www.sec.gov/Archives/...`.
- This surfaced while validating the `al-u4k` boundary-failed fixture, where URL coverage only appeared after switching fixture policy text to `sec.gov/Archives`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Baseline/sample policies that intend to catch SEC archive URLs use a regex that matches real `sec.gov/Archives` URLs.
- Add regression coverage proving the pattern matches.
close_reason: completed

title: Manifest module: AirlockManifest struct, canonical JSON emission
description:
## Goal
Implement the primary proof object — the airlock manifest. This is the most important output artifact. Every verification produces a manifest, even for BOUNDARY_FAILED.

## Deliverables

### src/manifest/mod.rs — Manifest types and emission

#### AirlockManifest struct
All fields from the plan's Artifact Model section:
- `manifest_version: String` — "airlock.v0"
- `boundary_mode: BoundaryMode` — from src/types.rs
- `policy_id: String`
- `policy_hash: String` — blake3:{hex}
- `claim_levels_evaluated: Vec<ClaimLevel>`
- `achieved_claim: ClaimLevel` — the verdict, from src/types.rs
- `upstream_artifact_inventory: Vec<UpstreamArtifact>` — from src/types.rs
- `system_prompt_hash: String` — blake3:{hex}, first-class field per invariant #2
- `prompt_payload_hash: String` — blake3:{hex}, deterministic core hash
- `prompt_provenance_hash: String` — blake3:{hex}
- `prompt_provenance_ref: String` — co-located path or pack member ID
- `request_payload_hash: String` — blake3:{hex}, full transport artifact hash
- `replay_ref: String` — co-located path for request payload
- `model_id: String`
- `adapter: String`
- `raw_document_present: bool`
- `filing_derived_text_present: bool`
- `findings: Vec<Finding>` — from src/types.rs
- `blocked_reasons: Vec<BlockedReason>` — from src/types.rs
- `provenance_summary: ProvenanceSummary` — aggregate fragment counts by boundary class
- `timestamp: String` — ISO 8601

#### ProvenanceSummary struct
```rust
pub struct ProvenanceSummary {
    pub total_fragments: usize,
    pub by_boundary_class: BTreeMap<String, usize>,
}
```
Built from prompt_provenance during manifest construction. The explain command reads this to render the fragment breakdown (e.g. "25 TELEMETRY, 2 DERIVED_TEXT") without needing the full provenance file.

Note: BoundaryMode, ClaimLevel, Finding, BlockedReason, UpstreamArtifact are defined in src/types.rs (al-1bo scaffold) and imported here. This avoids circular deps with scanner/assembler.

#### Emission
- `manifest.to_canonical_json() -> String` — uses sort_value() for deterministic output
- `manifest.hash() -> String` — blake3 of canonical JSON bytes
- `manifest.write_to(path: &Path) -> Result<(), std::io::Error>` — atomic write

#### Builder pattern
- `ManifestBuilder` for constructing manifests from scanner results + hash references
- Validates all required fields are present before build()
- Accepts PromptProvenance and computes ProvenanceSummary automatically

## Acceptance Criteria
- AirlockManifest contains every field from the plan's artifact model PLUS provenance_summary
- ProvenanceSummary.total_fragments equals the number of ProvenanceRecords
- ProvenanceSummary.by_boundary_class counts match actual provenance data
- Canonical JSON output has recursively sorted keys at every nesting level
- Same manifest struct produces identical JSON bytes across multiple serializations (determinism test)
- Manifest hash is deterministic (hash of canonical JSON)
- ManifestBuilder validates required fields (missing field → descriptive error)
- timestamp format is ISO 8601
- All hash fields match blake3:{hex} format
- Unit tests: construct manifest with all claim levels, verify JSON determinism, verify builder validation, verify provenance_summary computation

title: Phase A: verify binds request messages to the assembled prompt (REQUEST_UNBOUND)
description:
Parent: Airlock v1 epic. This is the P0 correctness hole.

REPRO (2026-09-02, fixtures/clean_telemetry_only): assemble in TELEMETRY_ONLY; build request = {model, messages: prompt.messages + [{role:user, content:'alice,123-45-6789,acct 4444-5555'}]}; verify --require-claim STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY -> exit 0, achieved_claim STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY. Only HTML/sec.gov injections are caught.

DESIGN: in src/scanner/mod.rs verify(): (1) extract request messages via the adapter for manifest.adapter (currently openai_chat_completions; adapter trait gains fn unwrap(&Value) -> Result<PromptView>). (2) Compare canonical JSON of each request message to the assembled prompt messages in order; system prompt compared by hash. Any extra, missing, reordered, or altered message -> finding {class: REQUEST_UNBOUND, path: messages[i], reason} and achieved_claim = BOUNDARY_FAILED. (3) Transport keys: adapter declares allowed top-level keys (model, temperature, max_tokens, response_format, tools?...); unknown keys -> REQUEST_UNBOUND finding (hidden adapter-side enrichments are in the threat model already). (4) Manifest records binding_status: BOUND | UNBOUND with details.

BACKWARD COMPAT: none needed (early development). Bump manifest_version to airlock.v0.2 and update schemas/airlock.v0.schema.json + fixtures.

TESTS: new fixture fixtures/request_unbound_pii/ reproducing the repro; reorder case; altered content case; extra transport key case; clean case still passes; determinism test unchanged. cmdrvl-gtm caller: its synthetic request copies prompt.messages so it stays BOUND - confirm in the gtm follow-up bead.

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): adapter trait gains fn unwrap(&Value) -> Result<PromptView {system, messages}> and fn transport_keys() -> &[&str]; binding compares JCS-canonical forms (see the RFC 8785 bead; until it lands use the existing canonicalizer, then swap). Manifest gains binding_status: BOUND|UNBOUND plus attestation: self_attested (this bead), transmitted (send), gated (gate) so consumers can distinguish a caller-supplied request from real bytes. explain prints attestation first.
acceptance_criteria: Appended, removed, reordered, or altered messages and undeclared transport keys yield REQUEST_UNBOUND and a BOUNDARY_FAILED manifest; the unchanged assembled request remains bound.

title: Project scaffold: Cargo.toml, main.rs, lib.rs, core utilities, build profile
description:
## Goal
Bootstrap the airlock Rust project with the full spine-tool scaffold. This is the foundation every other bead depends on.

## Deliverables

### Cargo.toml
- Package name: `airlock`
- Edition 2021, rust-version = "1.80"
- Pinned dependencies matching spine convention:
  - clap = { version = "=4.5.60", features = ["derive"] }
  - serde = { version = "=1.0.225", features = ["derive"] }
  - serde_json = "=1.0.143"
  - serde_yaml = "=0.9.34"
  - blake3 = "=1.8.2"
  - sha2 = "=0.10"
  - chrono = "=0.4.41"
  - regex = "=1.11"
- Dev dependencies:
  - assert_cmd = "2"
  - predicates = "3"
  - tempfile = "3"
  - jsonschema = "0.18" (or latest)
- Release profile: opt-level = "z", lto = true, codegen-units = 1, panic = "abort", strip = true

### src/main.rs
- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`
- Thin entrypoint: `fn main() -> ExitCode { ExitCode::from(airlock::run()) }`

### src/lib.rs
- `pub fn run() -> u8` — minimal stub that returns 0. Real dispatch added by al-jwl.

### src/types.rs — Shared domain types
These are used across policy, manifest, scanner, assembler, and provenance modules. Defined here to avoid circular dependencies.

```rust
// Boundary modes
pub enum BoundaryMode { Annotated, TelemetryOnly }
// Serializes as "ANNOTATED" / "TELEMETRY_ONLY"

// Claim levels (strict ordering)
pub enum ClaimLevel { BoundaryFailed, RawDocumentAbsent, StrictTelemetryOnly }
// Implements Ord: BoundaryFailed < RawDocumentAbsent < StrictTelemetryOnly
// Serializes as SCREAMING_SNAKE

// Finding — offending item detected during scanning
pub struct Finding {
    pub key_path: String,
    pub sample_value: Option<String>,  // truncated to 100 chars
    pub artifact_class: String,
    pub matched_rule: String,
}

// BlockedReason — why a stronger claim was not earned
pub struct BlockedReason {
    pub claim_attempted: ClaimLevel,
    pub reason: String,
    pub offending_paths: Vec<String>,
}

// UpstreamArtifact — an input that influenced the boundary crossing
pub struct UpstreamArtifact {
    pub path: String,
    pub content_hash: String,
    pub artifact_class: String,
}
```

All types derive Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone, PartialEq.

### src/hash.rs — Hashing utilities
- `blake3_hash(data: &[u8]) -> String` — returns `blake3:{hex}` spine format
- `sha256_hash(data: &[u8]) -> String` — returns `sha256:{hex}` fallback format
- `hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String, std::io::Error>` — read file bytes, return blake3 hash

### src/output.rs — Canonical JSON utilities
- `sort_value(v: serde_json::Value) -> Value` — recursive canonical JSON key sorting at all nesting levels
- `canonical_json(v: &Value) -> String` — sort then serialize
- `canonical_json_bytes(v: &Value) -> Vec<u8>` — for hashing

### src/cli/mod.rs + src/cli/exit.rs — CLI stub
- `pub const VERIFY_PASS: u8 = 0;`
- `pub const VERIFY_PARTIAL: u8 = 1;`
- `pub const REFUSAL: u8 = 2;`
- Empty mod.rs re-exporting exit codes

- tests/ directory (empty)
- .gitignore (target/, *.swp, etc.)

- `cargo fmt --check` clean

title: Verify command: end-to-end verification with manifest emission and --require-claim
description:
## Goal
Wire the verify subcommand end-to-end: load policy + prompt + provenance + request, run the scanner, emit airlock_manifest.json, support --require-claim gating, record witness.

## Deliverables

### Verify command handler

#### Flow
1. Load and validate policy file → RefusalEnvelope on failure
2. Read and parse prompt_payload.json → RefusalEnvelope on failure
3. Read and parse prompt_provenance.json → RefusalEnvelope on failure
4. Read and parse request.json → RefusalEnvelope on failure
5. Hash all input artifacts (blake3)
6. Determine boundary_mode from provenance metadata (or from flag if provided)
7. Call scanner::verify(policy, prompt, provenance, request, boundary_mode)
8. Build AirlockManifest with:
   - All hash references (policy, prompt, provenance, request, system prompt)
   - Upstream artifact inventory from provenance
   - Scanner results (findings, blocked_reasons, achieved_claim)
   - Boundary mode, model_id, adapter from provenance/request metadata
   - replay_ref and prompt_provenance_ref paths
   - Timestamp (ISO 8601)
9. Write airlock_manifest.json to --out path (canonical JSON)
10. Apply --require-claim gating:
    - If achieved_claim >= require_claim → exit 0 (VERIFY_PASS)
    - If achieved_claim < require_claim → exit 1 (VERIFY_PARTIAL)
    - Manifest is ALWAYS written regardless of gating result
11. Record witness (unless --no-witness):
    - outcome: VERIFIED or VERIFY_PARTIAL
    - inputs: all file paths+hashes
12. Print manifest JSON to stdout

#### Exit code logic (critical)
- BOUNDARY_FAILED verdict → exit 0 (tool ran correctly, produced honest manifest)
- BOUNDARY_FAILED + --require-claim RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT → exit 1 (claim below threshold)
- RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT + --require-claim RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT → exit 0
- RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT + --require-claim STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY → exit 1
- STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY + any --require-claim → exit 0

#### Error paths
- Any input file missing → RefusalEnvelope, exit 2
- Invalid JSON in any input → RefusalEnvelope, exit 2
- Policy parse failure → RefusalEnvelope, exit 2

## Acceptance Criteria
- End-to-end test: verify with clean inputs → manifest with correct claim
- Manifest is always emitted, even for BOUNDARY_FAILED
- --require-claim gates exit code correctly (all 5 combinations above)
- Manifest contains all fields from artifact model spec
- Manifest canonical JSON is deterministic
- Missing files → structured refusal
- Witness records VERIFIED or VERIFY_PARTIAL correctly
- --no-witness → no witness record
- Exit code 2 only for refusals, never for domain outcomes
close_reason: Implemented verify command wiring, manifest emission, require-claim gating, witness recording, and tests

title: OpenAI adapter: thin transport mapping from prompt_payload to request envelope
description:
## Goal
Implement the first thin transport adapter: OpenAI Chat Completions API format. The adapter maps (prompt_payload, transport_config) → request_payload. It MUST NOT inject semantic content.

## Deliverables

### src/adapter/mod.rs

#### TransportConfig struct
- `model_id: String` — e.g. "gpt-4", "o3"
- `temperature: Option<f64>`
- `max_tokens: Option<u32>`
- `response_format: Option<Value>` — vendor-specific response format
- `additional_params: Option<Map<String, Value>>` — pass-through for vendor-specific fields

#### Adapter trait (if multiple adapters later)
```rust
pub trait Adapter {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn wrap(&self, prompt_payload: &Value, config: &TransportConfig) -> Result<Value, RefusalEnvelope>;
}
```

#### OpenAI Chat Completions adapter
- Takes prompt_payload (system message + user message content)
- Wraps into OpenAI Chat Completions format:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "..."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "..."}
  ],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "response_format": {...}
}
```
- Adapter name: "openai_chat_completions"

#### Critical constraint: no semantic injection
- Adapters may reshape envelopes
- Adapters may NOT inject semantic content that lacks provenance coverage
- The adapter adds only transport-layer fields: model, temperature, max_tokens, response_format
- The content of messages comes entirely from prompt_payload

#### Request payload hashing
- The adapter output is the request_payload
- Caller hashes it with blake3 for the manifest's request_payload_hash

## Acceptance Criteria
- Adapter wraps prompt_payload into valid OpenAI Chat Completions format
- Adapter adds only transport fields, no semantic content
- Round-trip: unwrap the adapter output, content matches original prompt_payload
- Missing model_id → RefusalEnvelope
- adapter.name() returns "openai_chat_completions"
- Output JSON keys are canonical (sorted)
- Unit tests: basic wrap, verify no extra content beyond transport fields, missing config

title: Phase C: LOCAL_READS_CLEAN claim from veil session attestation
description:
Parent al-39t. Depends on al-33c and cross-repo veil attest bead (Track D).

WHY: a clean request does not prove the agent never read the document while assembling it. veil attest gives a signed per-session summary (reads attempted/denied, broker calls with output hashes, enforcement level, twin flag). Embedding it lets the manifest say 'no raw document entered the agent during assembly'.

WHAT: assemble/verify/send accept --session-attestation attest.json; airlock verifies its signature (veil public key), checks the session id matches the caller-declared session, and that every TOOL_RESULT fragment hash appears in the attestation's broker outputs; manifest gains local_reads {status: CLEAN|UNVERIFIED|VIOLATED, enforcement, twin, attestation_hash}. New claim ceiling label LOCAL_READS_CLEAN is reported alongside (not above) STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY: they are orthogonal axes and explain prints both.

TESTS: fixture attestations (clean, one denied read, hook-only vs sandboxed); mismatch session id -> UNVERIFIED; tool result not in broker outputs -> VIOLATED.

REFINEMENT ROUND 2: also depends on al-210 (TOOL_RESULT fragments are checked against the attestation's broker outputs).

title: Phase A: boundary classes MODEL_OUTPUT and TOOL_RESULT with conversation chains
description:
Parent al-39t. Depends on al-1ay.

WHY: agent loops are chains of crossings. Turn n's prompt legitimately contains turn n-1's model response and tool results. Without classes for those, either binding fails (extra content) or the loop bypasses airlock. The chain is what lets a whole session, not one call, carry a claim.

WHAT: (1) boundary classes {TELEMETRY, DERIVED_TEXT, MODEL_OUTPUT, TOOL_RESULT}. (2) assemble accepts --prior-manifest M and --response R: R's hash must equal M.transmission.response_hash (or the gate's recorded hash); its content is admitted as MODEL_OUTPUT fragments; TOOL_RESULT fragments must reference a veil derived-registry hash (~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/derived.jsonl) or a declared local artifact hash, else they are DERIVED_TEXT at best. (3) manifest gains chain {prior_manifest_hash, turn_index}; explain prints the chain. (4) Claim semantics: STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY allows MODEL_OUTPUT and registered TOOL_RESULT; unregistered tool results cap the claim at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT. (5) 'airlock chain verify <manifest>' walks back to turn 0 verifying each link.

TESTS: 3-turn fixture chain; tampered response hash breaks the chain; unregistered tool result caps the claim; determinism.

comments.author: IndigoOriole
comments.text:
IndigoOriole, al-210 start: findings and decisions I need before writing code. No al-210 code is written or committed. State checked at bdb1cdf (main = master).

Why I stopped to ask: the bead as written cannot be implemented literally, and four of the choices change what a claim means or change a released format. I would rather get rulings than build something I then have to undo.

FINDINGS (each checked in the repo, not assumed)
1. The response hash has nowhere to live in a manifest. The bead says R's hash must equal `M.transmission.response_hash` "(or the gate's recorded hash)". There is no `transmission` member in any manifest version (v0.3 members: bytes_crossed, attestation, not_crossed, signature), and one cannot exist in a manifest written by `verify`, because verify runs BEFORE the request is sent, so no response exists yet. docs/airlock_plan.md (the Boundary classes paragraph) repeats "hash recorded in manifest n-1", which has the same problem. The only artifact that records a response hash is the gate receipt (`airlock.gate.v1`: `response_hash`, plus `matched_manifest_hash` back to the manifest). So the real chain is manifest n-1 <- gate receipt n-1 (matched_manifest_hash) -> response hash -> turn n. Gate receipts are plain unsigned JSON files, so the response link is only as strong as the receipt.
2. The veil registry does not exist as an implementable contract. `~/.cmdrvl/state/veil/derived.jsonl` appears only as plan text (veil docs/plan.md line 525, item 9 of a numbered list). Nothing under veil/src reads or writes it and no record schema is defined, so airlock cannot read it today. The bead's other path, a "declared local artifact hash", is implementable.
3. The claim has no per-class input today. `derive_claim` (src/scanner/mod.rs) takes two booleans, raw_document_present and filing_derived_text_present. STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY currently means: TELEMETRY_ONLY mode, no raw document, no derived text, request bound, detectors did not block. Letting MODEL_OUTPUT through at the strict level means the strongest claim would cover free-form model text that no policy key admitted.
4. There is no response parsing anywhere. The `Adapter` trait has only `unwrap(request)`; the four adapters (anthropic_messages, gemini_generate_content, generic_json, openai_responses) unwrap requests. Admitting "R's content as MODEL_OUTPUT fragments" needs a response unwrapper per provider and a rule for which parts of a response become fragments (assistant text, tool_use blocks, refusals).
5. `chain {prior_manifest_hash, turn_index}` adds manifest members. By your ruling on al-33c (new members change manifest bytes, so a no-bump is dishonest) that means a version bump, and airlock.v0.3 only shipped today (0e3d979) with signed goldens. Folding the chain into v0.3 would redefine a released version.
6. `airlock chain verify <manifest>` "walks back to turn 0", but a manifest embeds only the prior manifest's hash, so verify needs somewhere to find prior manifests and receipts by hash.
7. `BoundaryClass` today is {Telemetry, DerivedText, Forbidden} (src/assembler/provenance.rs). The bead lists four classes and no Forbidden. Adding variants touches the prompt_provenance schema, explain's per-class summary and derive_claim.

DECISIONS NEEDED (answer each in one line; my recommendation first)
D1. Response anchor: take the response hash from the gate receipt, with `assemble --prior-receipt G --response R` (G.response_hash must equal blake3 of R's bytes, and G.matched_manifest_hash names the prior manifest), instead of `--prior-manifest` alone? Recommend yes. Say so if you want a different anchor; note the receipt is unsigned.
D2. Strict claim semantics for MODEL_OUTPUT. (a) as the bead says: STRICT admits MODEL_OUTPUT outright. (b) screened-clean: MODEL_OUTPUT caps the claim at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT unless the response itself was screened by the policy's forbidden patterns and detector packs and found clean, and only then does STRICT admit it. Recommend (b), because (a) lets unscreened model text carry the top claim.
D3. TOOL_RESULT: implement only the declared-local-artifact-hash path now (a tool result is TOOL_RESULT only if its hash is declared; otherwise it caps the claim at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT) and defer the veil registry until veil defines the record format? Recommend yes. Who owns defining the veil format?
D4. Manifest version: bump the chain members to airlock.v0.4, with the gate accepting v0.2 to v0.4 during the transition and existing goldens untouched, as with v0.3? Recommend yes.
D5. chain verify lookup: `airlock chain verify <manifest> --manifest-dir DIR [--receipt-dir DIR]`, the same style as the gate's strict-manifest `--manifest-dir`. It would check, per link: the prior manifest's hash matches, turn_index is prior+1, receipt.matched_manifest_hash equals the prior manifest's hash, receipt.response_hash equals the hash of the response the turn admitted, and the signature when the manifest is signed and a key is given. OK?
D6. Providers for the first response unwrappers. Recommend openai_responses and anthropic_messages first (generic_json and gemini after). Fragment rule: assistant text and tool_use blocks only. OK?

PROPOSED COMMITS once D1 to D6 are answered (one at a time, each with real tests, mutation checks and a clean-export run)
- D-a: BoundaryClass variants, response unwrappers, `assemble --response/--prior-receipt` producing MODEL_OUTPUT fragments and provenance records, claim rule per D2.
- D-b: TOOL_RESULT by declared artifact hash, with the claim cap.
- D-c: chain members, v0.4 bump, schema, gate accepts v0.2 to v0.4, new goldens only, explain prints the chain.
- D-d: `airlock chain verify`.
- D-e: README and operator.json.
Tests from the bead: 3-turn fixture chain; tampered response hash breaks the chain; unregistered tool result caps the claim; determinism. I would add a test that a response containing a forbidden pattern fails the boundary, for D2(b).

FILES: src/assembler/*, src/scanner/mod.rs, src/adapter/*, src/commands/{assemble,verify,explain}.rs, src/manifest/mod.rs, src/cli/mod.rs, schemas/, operator.json, README. I will reserve exact paths before editing. PlumShore has not messaged about any of these since the 13:15 UTC archive-command message, but a bead named "coordinate files with Pane A" needs your word on whether Pane A is touching src/scanner/mod.rs or the adapters right now.

STILL OPEN ON al-33c: C5 (prev_hash witness chain), assessed as not cheap in the C4 comment, and the C3 question of whether gate should verify signatures.

Not independently verified: all of the above is from reading the repo and veil's plan; I ran nothing for it beyond grep and reading.

comments.author: IndigoOriole
comments.text:
IndigoOriole, recording the ORCHESTRATOR rulings on al-210 (orchestrator's calls under the P0/P1 session; each takes my recommendation from the findings comment):

D1 YES. The response anchor is the gate receipt: `assemble --prior-receipt G --response R`, with G.response_hash equal to the hash of R's bytes and G.matched_manifest_hash naming the prior manifest. The docs must say the receipt is unsigned.
D2 (b), screened-clean. MODEL_OUTPUT caps the claim at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT unless the response itself was screened by the policy's forbidden patterns and detector packs and found clean; only then may STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY admit it. Described by the orchestrator as the honest, stricter claim.
D3 YES. TOOL_RESULT by declared local artifact hash only (an undeclared tool result caps the claim at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT). The veil registry format belongs to the veil repo; I do not define it here.
D4 YES. The chain members go in airlock.v0.4. The gate accepts v0.2 to v0.4. Existing goldens stay untouched; new goldens only.
D5 YES as proposed: `airlock chain verify <manifest> --manifest-dir DIR [--receipt-dir DIR]`, with the per-link checks listed in the findings comment.
D6 YES. openai_responses and anthropic_messages response unwrappers first; assistant text and tool_use blocks only.
Go with D-a, one commit at a time, with mutation checks and a clean-export run.

ALSO RULED (al-33c): the gate verifies the signature when a manifest is signed AND a key is configured, and never requires one. Done as its own small commit, before D-a.

My reading of "a key is configured", stated now so it can be reversed: an explicit `--pubkey PATH` on `airlock gate`, or failing that the default public key file `~/.cmdrvl/secrets/airlock/ed25519.pub` when it exists. A configured key that cannot be loaded is a startup refusal, not a silent skip. An unsigned manifest is always accepted by this rule. I will say this again in the commit's evidence comment.

ORDER OF WORK: gate signature check (al-33c), then D-a (al-210).

comments.author: IndigoOriole
comments.text:
al-210 D-a DESIGN (IndigoOriole), written BEFORE any D-a code. al-210 claimed (in_progress). Rulings D1-D6 stand. Base 22e480f (main = master). Closing is the orchestrator's.

SCOPE OF D-a
MODEL_OUTPUT only: `assemble --prior-receipt G --response R --response-adapter A`, the response unwrappers for openai_responses and anthropic_messages, the MODEL_OUTPUT provenance class, and the D2(b) claim rule in verify. TOOL_RESULT (D-b), chain members + v0.4 (D-c), `chain verify` (D-d), docs (D-e) follow as separate commits. I am adding only the MODEL_OUTPUT enum variant now, TOOL_RESULT arrives with its producer in D-b, so no variant exists without a user.

FINDINGS FROM READING THE CODE (these change the shape of D-a)
1. OpenAI Responses refuses structured assistant content (openai_responses.rs wrap: "cannot carry structured assistant content"), and, as I understand the Anthropic Messages API (not checked against current docs, the repo does not enforce it), the first non-system message must be `user`. So carrying the prior response as `assistant` messages does not work across both adapters, and a trailing assistant message means prefill/continue semantics on Anthropic, which is not what an agent loop wants.
2. `provenance_gap` is advisory by design and pinned by a test (`provenance_gap_is_recorded_without_degrading_claim`). So if verify decided "model output present" from provenance labels, deleting the MODEL_OUTPUT records would lift the claim cap. The cap must be decided from the prompt's structure.
3. `AllowRule.boundary_class` is an override read from policy YAML. Adding the variant means a policy author could write `boundary_class: MODEL_OUTPUT` on an input field and launder a label. classify_rule must refuse it.
4. The bead's original wording (`M.transmission.response_hash`) is partly implementable now: al-b16 added `transmission.response_hash` to manifests that `send` writes. My earlier finding 1 was stale on that. D1 ruled the gate receipt, and I am building exactly that. QUESTION FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR (not blocking): for flows that use `send` with no gate, do you want `--prior-manifest M` (response hash from M.transmission) accepted as a second anchor? D-c needs `--prior-manifest` anyway for turn_index, so it is cheap there. Default if I hear nothing: not added.

DESIGN
- The prior response enters the prompt as quoted material in the user message under one reserved key: `messages[1].content.prior_turn.model_output = [{"kind":"text","text":...} | {"kind":"tool_use","id":...,"name":...,"input":...}]`. Indices of every existing path are unchanged, and with no `--response` the output is byte-identical to today (goldens untouched). `prior_turn` is reserved: an allowed key starting with it is refused at assemble.
- Fragment rule per D6: text and tool_use only. Reasoning/thinking, refusals and other block types are NOT admitted (dropping is the safe direction); a response with no admissible block is refused so the chain cannot silently advance on nothing. OpenAI function-call `arguments` (a JSON string) is parsed into `input` when it is valid JSON and kept as a string when it is not, so it is scanned either way.
- Receipt checks (D1, receipt unsigned, the docs will say so): gate_version is airlock.gate.v1, not blocked, upstream_status 2xx, `response_hash` present and equal to blake3 of R's bytes, `matched_manifest_hash` present. Any failure is a structured refusal and nothing is written. No new refusal code: these use E_BAD_INPUT with `detail.field`.
- Provenance: every leaf copied from the response is a record with boundary_class MODEL_OUTPUT, source_artifact_hash = the response hash, source_path = the location in the response, policy_rule_id `chain.model_output`, admitted in both modes. The `kind` tags are template records (TELEMETRY), like the role records.
- verify, D2(b): model output is "present" when any message's content is an object with a `prior_turn` key (structural, not from provenance). Claim: raw/unbound/detector-blocked still BOUNDARY_FAILED. If model output is present the claim is capped at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT unless it is SCREENED CLEAN, which I define as: at least one detector pack is enabled and not warn-only AND no detector finding (blocking or warn-only) lies under `prior_turn`. Forbidden patterns/keys apply to it as to every other text and fail the boundary. My reading of "screened by the policy's forbidden patterns and detector packs": a policy with no blocking detector pack does not screen free-form model text, so the cap applies. That is the stricter reading and it keeps D2(b) from being vacuous. Say so if you want the looser one.
- Side effect to disclose: a hand-built prompt with a `prior_turn` key now also gets the cap, and was previously uncapped.

PREDICTIONS (before running anything)
T1 assemble with a text response (each adapter): prompt carries prior_turn.model_output, text leaf recorded MODEL_OUTPUT, no coverage refusal. T2 same inputs twice: byte-identical prompt and provenance. T3 response with one byte altered: refusal, no files written. T4 blocked receipt / missing response_hash / 500 status / wrong gate_version: each a refusal. T5 policy `boundary_class: MODEL_OUTPUT` and allowed key `prior_turn.x`: each refused. T6 verify TELEMETRY_ONLY + model output + no detectors: RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT (cap). T7 same + blocking packs, clean: STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY. T8 same + AWS-shaped token in the response: BOUNDARY_FAILED. T9 packs all warn-only and a hit in the response: capped, not failed. T10 forbidden pattern (raw_html) in the response with no detectors: BOUNDARY_FAILED. T11 provenance MODEL_OUTPUT records deleted: claim unchanged from T6.
MUTATIONS I WILL RUN, each predicted: M1 cap removed from derive_claim: T6 fails, T7 still passes. M2 "screened" = any pack incl. warn-only: T9 fails. M3 receipt-hash comparison removed: T3 fails. M4 classify_rule accepts MODEL_OUTPUT: T5 policy case fails. M5 presence read from provenance labels instead of structure: T11 fails.

NOT IN D-a: TOOL_RESULT, chain members, v0.4, chain verify, explain chain output, README. Not independently verified: this is design from reading, no D-a code exists yet.

al-210 D-b design (IndigoOriole), posted BEFORE code. D-a is delivered at 069b9bd (CI green, evidence comment above). No D-b code exists yet. Reading checked at 7e14f69.

THE ONE DECISION D3 LEFT OPEN: where "declared" lives.
D3 says a tool result is TOOL_RESULT only by a declared local artifact hash, else the claim caps at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT. If assemble hashed whatever file it was handed and called that "declared", every tool result would be declared and the cap could never fire: that is self-certification. The declaration has to come from something independent of the assembled prompt. I chose the POLICY: it is operator-authored, `verify` already reads it, and its resolved hash is already bound into the manifest.
- New optional policy key `declared_tool_results: [{artifact_hash: "blake3:<64 lowercase hex>", description?: string}]`.
- Format impact, all additive: schemas/airlock_policy.schema.json gains the property (the schema is additionalProperties:false, so this is a real format change). Existing policies are valid and their resolved hash is unchanged (the field is skipped when empty; the existing goldens must pass untouched, and I will say so with the run). `version` stays airlock.v0. An OLDER airlock refuses a policy that uses the key (deny_unknown_fields), so it fails closed, not silently weaker. `extends` merges by union on artifact_hash. The hash set is sorted before hashing, so entry order does not change the policy hash. Malformed hashes are refused as E_BAD_POLICY with the field name.
- Rejected: declaration only on the assemble command line (verify could not re-check it, so the cap would rest on labels), and a separate declarations file (that invents a registry format, which D3 leaves to veil). Reversible: one optional key.

CLI AND PROMPT
- `assemble ... --tool-result TOOL_USE_ID=PATH`, repeatable, only together with the three chain flags. The artifact must be UTF-8 text and is embedded VERBATIM as a string, so blake3(file bytes) == blake3(content.as_bytes()) and verify can recompute the hash from the prompt alone. A non-UTF-8 artifact is refused. Each id must name a tool_use in the response given with --response; an unknown or duplicate id is refused (E_BAD_INPUT, nothing written). Prompt order follows the response's tool_use order, not flag order, so the bytes are deterministic.
- Prompt: prior_turn.tool_results = [{kind:"tool_result", tool_use_id, content}], a sibling of model_output. kind is a TELEMETRY template record; tool_use_id is MODEL_OUTPUT (copied from the response); content is TOOL_RESULT (source_artifact_hash = the artifact hash, rule chain.tool_result, COPY, both modes) when its hash is declared, else DERIVED_TEXT (rule chain.tool_result.undeclared; the bead's "DERIVED_TEXT at best").

CLAIM (decided in verify from the prompt's structure and the policy, never from labels; D-a's lesson, provenance_gap stays advisory)
- A tool result is declared iff blake3(content) is in the policy's declared set. Any tool_results entry that is not declared, including a malformed one, caps the claim at RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT. The blocked reason names messages[1].content.prior_turn.tool_results[k].
- Declaring is not screening. Tool results sit under prior_turn, so they inherit the D-a model-output screen: STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY with tool results needs all of (a) every tool result declared, (b) a blocking detector pack, (c) no detector hit under prior_turn. A blocking hit still fails the boundary. If both (a) and another condition fail, one blocked reason names both.
- Out of scope per D3: the veil derived-registry format.

TESTS (real binary) AND MUTATIONS, predictions written before each run
Tests: declared artifact + blocking pack reaches STRICT with the exact prompt and provenance map; undeclared caps and says why; a one-byte change to the artifact after declaring caps; relabeling or deleting the tool-result provenance labels does not move the claim; declared without a blocking pack is capped by the model-output reason, not the tool-result one; both reasons together; secret in a tool result fails the boundary under a blocking pack; refusals (unknown id, duplicate id, non-UTF-8, malformed spec, flags without the chain trio, missing file); flag order does not change the bytes; policy load/extends/malformed-hash/hash-stability unit tests; adapter wrap/unwrap restores the tool results exactly.
Mutations: (1) treat every tool result as declared; (2) hash the wrong bytes (trimmed content); (3) order by CLI not by response; (4) drop the unknown-id check; (5) read declared-ness from provenance labels; (6) do not sort the declared set before hashing; (7) skip the UTF-8 check.

The MODEL_OUTPUT/TOOL_RESULT tamper-matrix rows are planned after D-d, when the chain-verify cells exist; I will add the cells that already work (assemble refusals, the cap) in the same change so nothing waits on a later bead.

ASK (non-blocking, I proceed on D3 as written): undeclared tool results CROSS with a capped claim, they are not excluded in TELEMETRY_ONLY the way derived text is. I chose crossing because excluding would silently drop a result the agent needs for its next call, and D3 says "caps the claim". Say so if you wanted exclusion.

comments.author: IndigoOriole
comments.text:
IndigoOriole, al-210 D-c DESIGN (posted before code, per D-a and D-b). D-b is evidenced at fced7aa. Two points go beyond the D1-D6 rulings; both are marked. I proceed on the defaults unless redirected.

RULED, APPLIED AS WRITTEN (D4)
- Chain members live in airlock.v0.4. The gate accepts v0.2 to v0.4. Existing goldens are untouched; new goldens only.
- Member: `chain: {prior_manifest_hash, turn_index}`.

DESIGN
1. WHEN A MANIFEST IS v0.4: exactly when it carries `chain`. A manifest with no chain stays airlock.v0.3 and is byte-identical to today, so no existing golden or manifest hash moves. v0.4 = every v0.3 member plus `chain`; v0.4 REQUIRES chain, v0.2 and v0.3 must NOT have it (schema, gate loader and explain agree). Turn 0 is a manifest with no chain member; the first chained manifest has turn_index 1. turn_index >= 1, prior_manifest_hash is `blake3:` + 64 lowercase hex.
2. WHERE THE LINK TRAVELS (beyond the rulings): `verify` writes the manifest but only `assemble` sees the receipt. I put the link in prompt_provenance.json as an optional top-level `chain` member (skipped when absent, so non-chained provenance bytes are unchanged; schema updated). `verify` and `send` already read and hash that file, so neither gets a new flag and the member cannot be silently dropped between steps. The manifest member is then covered twice: by the manifest signature and by prompt_provenance_hash. Alternative rejected: a `--chain` side file like `--not-crossed`, because omitting it silently yields a root manifest for a chained prompt.
3. WHERE turn_index COMES FROM (beyond the rulings, the one deviation from D1's CLI shape): the receipt names the prior manifest by hash only, so it cannot carry an index. I add `assemble --prior-manifest M`, required with the other chain flags (`--tool-result` now needs all four). assemble loads M (a supported version, else E_BAD_INPUT `prior_manifest.version`), requires M.hash() == receipt.matched_manifest_hash (else E_BAD_INPUT `prior_manifest.hash`, so a receipt paired with the wrong manifest is caught BEFORE anything crosses), and sets turn_index = M.chain.turn_index + 1, or 1 when M has no chain. Alternative rejected: a typed `--turn-index N`, because a typo would surface only at `chain verify`, after the request had already been sent. If you prefer `--turn-index`, it is a small swap. M's signature is not checked at assemble; `chain verify` (D-d) does that.
4. verify and send REFUSE a provenance/prompt mismatch: provenance.chain present with no prompt_provenance `prior_turn` in the prompt, or a prompt with `prior_turn` and no provenance.chain. Reason: otherwise a manifest that took model output from an earlier turn could present as turn 0 and cut the chain short, and `chain verify` ("walk back to turn 0") would stop at it. This keeps "no chain member means root" true. The claim itself is still derived structurally from the prompt, unchanged.
5. SIGNING: sign and verify-manifest accept v0.4; the signature covers `chain` (it covers the whole canonical manifest minus `signature`). A v0.4 manifest with chain stripped or altered fails verification when signed.
6. GATE: strict-manifest loader accepts v0.2, v0.3, v0.4. v0.3 and v0.4 both require bytes_crossed and attestation. v0.4 without chain, or v0.3 with chain, is refused at start. The AirlockManifest struct gains `chain`, so the gate's re-hash (manifest.hash() from the parsed struct) includes it: without that, a chain member would silently vanish from the hash the gate stamps into receipts as matched_manifest_hash.
7. EXPLAIN prints the chain for v0.4 (text and --json): turn_index and prior_manifest_hash. v0.2 and v0.3 output is unchanged.
8. NEW GOLDENS: fixtures/chain/ gets an unsigned and a signed v0.4 manifest from a real two-turn run, and the test checks them byte for byte. The signed one's signature is derived independently (same method as expected_manifest_v0_3_signed.json, see tests/signing.rs header), not by this binary's signer.
9. Existing D-a and D-b tests get a real turn-0 manifest (assemble then verify) instead of a made-up receipt hash, so the receipt's matched_manifest_hash is the hash of a real file. That changes the test helper, not any assertion.

TESTS PLANNED: v0.3 output byte-identical for non-chained input (control); chained run gives v0.4 with the right member for turn 1 and turn 2 (index 2 from a chained M); wrong manifest for the receipt is refused before any output is written; unsupported or unreadable M refused; verify and send mismatch refusals in both directions; sign then strip or alter chain fails verify-manifest; gate accepts v0.2, v0.3, v0.4 and refuses v0.4-without-chain and v0.3-with-chain; schema accepts and rejects the same shapes the loader does; explain output; goldens. Mutation checks with predictions written to a FILE before each run this time (I did not keep them for D-b; see D-b disclosures).

NOT IN D-c: `airlock chain verify` (D-d), README and operator.json (D-e), tamper-matrix rows.

QUESTION FOR D-d, NON-BLOCKING: D5 checks "receipt.response_hash equals the hash of the response the turn admitted". The manifest does not hold that hash. My default: `chain verify` finds each turn's provenance in --manifest-dir via the manifest's prompt_provenance_ref, requires its blake3 to equal manifest.prompt_provenance_hash, and takes the response hash from the source_artifact_hash of its chain.model_output records. The alternative is adding response_hash to the chain member, which changes the member set you ruled, so I am NOT doing it unless you say so.

NEXT: D-c as above, unless you redirect.

title: Witness module: spine ledger protocol, append/query/last/count
description:
## Goal
Implement the spine witness ledger protocol. Airlock records a witness entry for eligible invocations (assemble, verify) and exposes the standard query surface (query, last, count).

## Deliverables

### src/witness/mod.rs

#### Witness record format (witness.v0)
```json
{
  "witness_version": "witness.v0",
  "tool": "airlock",
  "command": "verify",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "outcome": "VERIFIED",
  "exit_code": 0,
  "inputs": [
    {"path": "policy.yaml", "hash": "blake3:abc..."},
    {"path": "prompt.json", "hash": "blake3:def..."}
  ],
  "params": {"boundary_mode": "ANNOTATED", "require_claim": null},
  "stdout_hash": "blake3:ghi...",
  "stdout_bytes": 4096
}
```

#### Ledger path resolution
1. `EPISTEMIC_WITNESS` env var (if set)
2. `~/.epistemic/witness.jsonl` (default)
3. Create parent directories if needed

#### Recording policy (v0)
- Record for: `assemble`, `verify`
- Do NOT record for: `witness` subcommands, `--describe`, `--schema`, `--version`
- `explain` is non-recording in v0

#### Outcome mapping
- `assemble` → ASSEMBLED or REFUSAL
- `verify` → VERIFIED, VERIFY_PARTIAL, or REFUSAL

#### Append behavior
- `append_witness(record: WitnessRecord) -> Result<(), WitnessError>`
- Append one JSONL line to ledger file
- **CRITICAL**: append failure MUST NOT change domain exit semantics
  - If append fails, log to stderr, but return the original domain exit code
  - Never let a witness I/O error override a successful domain result

#### --no-witness support
- When `--no-witness` flag is present, skip append entirely
- Clean, early opt-out path

#### Query surface
- `query(filters: WitnessFilters) -> Vec<WitnessRecord>`
- `last() -> Option<WitnessRecord>`
- `count(filters: WitnessFilters) -> usize`

#### WitnessFilters
- `tool: Option<String>` (default: "airlock")
- `since: Option<DateTime>`
- `until: Option<DateTime>`
- `outcome: Option<String>`
- `input_hash: Option<String>` (substring match)
- `limit: Option<usize>`

#### Query exit semantics
- exit 0: successful query with matches
- exit 1: successful query with no matches
- exit 2: ledger error or refusal

## Acceptance Criteria
- Append writes valid JSONL line to ledger
- Append failure does not change domain exit code (critical test)
- --no-witness skips append entirely
- Ledger path resolves from env, then default
- Query filters work: by outcome, by date range, by input hash substring
- last() returns most recent record
- count() returns correct count with filters
- Query on empty/missing ledger returns 0 matches (exit 1), not error
- Unit tests: append, append failure isolation, query filters, last, count, empty ledger
close_reason: Implemented witness ledger, query helpers, best-effort append semantics, and tests

title: Policy module: AirlockPolicy types, YAML parsing, policy hashing
description:
## Goal
Implement the policy engine that defines what is allowed and forbidden at the model boundary. This is the rule substrate that the assembler and scanner operate against.

## Deliverables

### src/policy/types.rs — Policy types
```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct AirlockPolicy {
    pub policy_id: String,
    pub version: String,
    pub allowed_keys: Vec<AllowRule>,
    pub forbidden_keys: Vec<String>,
    pub forbidden_patterns: Vec<ForbiddenPattern>,
    pub derived_text_paths: Vec<String>,
    pub claim_levels: Vec<String>,
}
```

- `AllowRule` struct: key path, optional description, optional boundary class override
- `DenyRule` / `ForbiddenPattern` struct: pattern (regex string), description, artifact class
- All types derive Serialize, Deserialize, Debug, Clone

### src/policy/mod.rs — Parsing and hashing
- `load_policy(path: &Path) -> Result<AirlockPolicy, RefusalEnvelope>` — parse YAML, validate required fields
- `hash_policy(path: &Path) -> String` — read raw bytes, compute `blake3:{hex}` hash of the file content
- Policy validation: policy_id non-empty, version non-empty, at least one allow rule, claim_levels non-empty and must be valid enum values
- On parse failure, return structured RefusalEnvelope with code E_BAD_POLICY

### Example policy file: rules/tournament_baseline.yaml
A complete example policy matching the BDC tournament reference:
- Allow: family_id, current_strategy, allowed_toggles, max_proposals, benchmark_summary, unresolved_failure_fields, recent_lineage_rows, heuristic_reference, mutator_context (with sub-field rules)
- Forbid keys: html_path, section_html, pdf_path, page_images
- Forbid patterns: raw HTML markup (<[a-z][^>]*>), SEC archive URLs (sec.gov/Archives)
- Derived text paths: mutator_context.challenge_observation, mutator_context.challenge_profile.header_surfaces, mutator_context.challenge_profile.layout_notes
- Claim levels: BOUNDARY_FAILED, RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT, STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY

## Acceptance Criteria
- Round-trip test: serialize → deserialize → serialize produces identical YAML
- Policy hash is deterministic (same file = same hash every time)
- Bad YAML returns RefusalEnvelope, not panic
- Missing required fields return clear refusal
- Forbidden patterns compile as valid regex (test with known good and bad patterns)
- Example policy file validates successfully
- Unit tests cover: valid policy, missing policy_id, invalid regex pattern, empty allowed_keys
notes: Implementation is in place in src/policy/mod.rs, src/policy/types.rs, and rules/tournament_baseline.yaml. Local formatting succeeded via rustfmt on the policy files. Crate-level verification is currently blocked outside this bead by edition-2021-incompatible let-chains in src/witness/mod.rs after earlier src/lib.rs parse errors were resolved. Routed both failures to the owning agents via Agent Mail.

title: Assemble command: end-to-end prompt assembly with file I/O and witness
description:
## Goal
Wire the assemble subcommand end-to-end: load policy, read input files, run the assembler, emit prompt_payload.json + prompt_provenance.json, record witness.

## Deliverables

### Assemble command handler (in src/lib.rs or src/cli/ dispatch)

#### Flow
1. Load and validate policy file → RefusalEnvelope on failure
2. Read and hash each --input file → RefusalEnvelope on missing/invalid
3. Read system prompt file if --system-prompt provided, else use empty/default
4. Parse --boundary-mode (ANNOTATED default)
5. Call assembler::assemble(policy, inputs, system_prompt, boundary_mode)
6. Write prompt_payload.json to --out path (canonical JSON)
7. Write prompt_provenance.json to --provenance-out path (canonical JSON)
8. Record witness (unless --no-witness):
   - outcome: ASSEMBLED
   - inputs: policy path+hash, each input path+hash
   - stdout_hash: hash of prompt_payload.json bytes
   - stdout_bytes: byte length of prompt_payload.json
9. Print confirmation to stdout (the prompt_payload.json content)
10. Exit 0

#### Error paths
- Policy load failure → RefusalEnvelope (E_BAD_POLICY), exit 2
- Input file missing → RefusalEnvelope (E_MISSING_FILE), exit 2
- Input file invalid JSON → RefusalEnvelope (E_BAD_INPUT), exit 2
- Output path not writable → RefusalEnvelope (E_BAD_INPUT), exit 2
- Witness append failure → stderr warning, but still exit 0

## Acceptance Criteria
- End-to-end test: assemble with valid policy + inputs → prompt_payload.json + prompt_provenance.json exist and are valid JSON
- Determinism test: run twice, both output files are byte-identical
- Multiple --input files all appear in upstream_artifact_inventory of provenance
- Missing policy → structured refusal with E_BAD_POLICY
- Missing input → structured refusal with E_MISSING_FILE
- --no-witness → no witness record appended
- --boundary-mode TELEMETRY_ONLY strips derived text fields from output
- Exit code is always 0 on success, 2 on refusal

title: Explain command: human-readable manifest rendering
description:
## Goal
Implement `airlock explain --manifest <PATH>` — renders a manifest into a concise, human-readable verdict summary. Stakeholders should understand the proof without reading raw JSON.

## Deliverables

### Explain command handler

#### Flow
1. Load and parse airlock_manifest.json → RefusalEnvelope on failure
2. Render human-readable output to stdout

#### Output format (from README example)
```text
AIRLOCK

Claim achieved: RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT
Boundary mode: ANNOTATED

Raw document artifacts: absent
Derived filing text: present

Why strict telemetry-only was not earned:
  - mutator_context.challenge_observation
  - mutator_context.challenge_profile.layout_notes[0]

Prompt provenance:
  - 27 prompt fragments emitted
  - 25 TELEMETRY
  - 2 DERIVED_TEXT

Policy: tournament_baseline (blake3:abc123...)
Manifest hash: blake3:def456...
```

#### Rendering rules
- Always show: claim achieved, boundary mode
- Always show: raw_document_present, filing_derived_text_present (as human words)
- If BOUNDARY_FAILED: show "Boundary violation detected:" followed by findings
- If not STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY: show "Why strict telemetry-only was not earned:" with blocked_reasons
- Show prompt provenance summary: total fragments, count by boundary_class
- Show policy_id and policy_hash
- Show manifest hash
- Do NOT show timestamps, full upstream inventory, or other verbose fields (those are in the JSON)
- Non-recording in v0 (no witness append for explain)

#### Exit code
- exit 0: manifest loaded and rendered
- exit 2: manifest file missing or invalid (RefusalEnvelope)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Explain renders each claim level correctly (BOUNDARY_FAILED, RAW_DOCUMENT_ABSENT, STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY)
- Explain shows blocked reasons when claim < STRICT_TELEMETRY_ONLY
- Explain shows findings when BOUNDARY_FAILED
- Missing manifest → structured refusal
- Invalid manifest JSON → structured refusal
- Output is plain text on stdout, not JSON
- No witness recording for explain
- Unit tests: explain for each claim level, explain for missing manifest
close_reason: Implemented explain command with structured refusal fallback and human-readable rendering

title: Phase A: manifest bytes_crossed, not_crossed inventory, and Ed25519 signature
description:
Parent: Airlock v1 epic. Depends on PA1 (manifest version bump).

WHY: collateral promises 'how many bytes crossed', a 'what crossed and what did NOT cross split', and a 'signed declaration'. The manifest has none. Make them true rather than editing the pitch down.

DESIGN: (1) bytes_crossed: byte length of the canonical request JSON that verify hashed (and, after Phase B, the exact bytes sent). (2) not_crossed[]: during assemble, every input field that was dropped (not in allowed_keys), every forbidden key stripped, and every derived_text path excluded in TELEMETRY_ONLY mode is recorded as {path, source_artifact, sha256 of the value, reason}. Values are never stored. verify copies the list into the manifest so explain can print the negative inventory. (3) signature: 'airlock keygen' writes an Ed25519 keypair under ~/.cmdrvl/secrets/airlock/ (veil already protects that subtree); verify signs the canonical manifest (minus the signature field) and records signer public key fingerprint; 'airlock verify-manifest <manifest> [--pubkey]' checks it and refuses on mismatch; --no-sign for CI. Use ed25519-dalek pinned like other deps.

TESTS: schema updates; signature roundtrip; tamper-after-sign detection; not_crossed golden for annotated_mode fixture; explain shows both lists.

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): add fragment_merkle_root: each prompt fragment is a leaf H(class || path || JCS(value)); provenance entries carry inclusion proofs (sibling hash path) so an auditor verifies one fragment's provenance without seeing the others (selective disclosure: a manifest redacted to a subset of fragments still verifies). 'airlock verify-manifest' checks signature, root, and any proofs present, standalone (public key + manifest, no policy). Add 'attestation' and 'binding_status' to the schema (from al-1ay). explain --auditor prints the customs declaration: attestation mode, what crossed (fragments by class with counts), what did not (not_crossed[]), claim, signer fingerprint, ledger inclusion (if the verifiable-log bead has landed).
notes:
2026-11-24 scope trim for v1 velocity:
- v1 ships: `bytes_crossed`, `not_crossed[]`, `attestation` provenance (`self_attested|transmitted|gated`), `prev_hash`-chained witness entries, and Ed25519 signature over RFC 8785 JCS (`airlock verify-manifest`).
- Defer `fragment_merkle_root` / selective-disclosure per-fragment inclusion proofs to v1.5 so Phase A ships without blocking the wire gate.

comments.text:
IndigoOriole, al-33c gate signature check, its own small commit f88fa79 (per the orchestrator ruling: verify when the manifest is signed AND a key is configured, never require one). Not closing the bead: C5 stays open, see the end.

WHAT IT DOES (strict-manifest mode only)
- Each manifest in --manifest-dir that carries a `signature` is checked against the configured key with the same strict Ed25519 check `verify-manifest` uses (signing::verify_value, on the parsed JSON, so a member this build does not know is still covered).
- "A key is configured", as I stated in the rulings comment so it can be reversed: an explicit `--pubkey PATH`, or failing that the default public key file ~/.cmdrvl/secrets/airlock/ed25519.pub when it exists. If neither exists, no key is configured and nothing is checked; the gate says so on stderr ("no signing key configured; manifest signatures are not checked") and `GET /airlock/health` reports `signature_key: null`.
- A configured key that cannot be loaded (named file missing, not a key, or an unreadable default file) is a startup refusal (exit 2, stderr names the problem, "refusing to start"), not a silent skip.
- A signed manifest that does not verify under the configured key (altered after signing, or signed by another key) is a startup refusal that names the file. I chose refusal over skipping the file: skipping would turn a tampered or wrong-key manifest into a quiet "no matching manifest" 403 on one request class, which hides the cause. This matches how the gate already treats an invalid manifest in the directory. Say so if you would rather it skip and warn.
- An unsigned manifest is always accepted, with or without a key. A genuine v0.2 manifest has no `signature` member, so it is unaffected. A v0.2 manifest that DOES carry a `signature` member is refused at startup when a key is configured ("only airlock.v0.3 manifests carry a signature; this one is airlock.v0.2"), the same way verify-manifest treats it. I checked that by hand with the built binary (a v0.2 golden plus a made-up signature member, --pubkey set: exit 2 with that message); there is NO committed test for it. With no key configured it is accepted like any other manifest.
- `--pubkey` is refused in policy-proxy mode, like --manifest-dir.
- `GET /airlock/health` (strict-manifest) gains `signature_key`: the blake3 fingerprint of the key in use, or null. This is a new member of an existing JSON body; the existing health test was updated for it.
- The check runs once, when manifests are loaded at startup. A manifest file changed while the gate runs is not rechecked (the gate never reloaded the directory; this commit does not add that).

TESTS (real `airlock gate` binary, real `airlock keygen` for the second key, HOME and USERPROFILE removed from every gate command so no default key leaks in from whoever runs the tests; tests that want a default key point HOME at a temp dir)
10 new tests in tests/gate_strict.rs: signed by the configured key is forwarded (and health/stderr show the fingerprint); altered after signing refuses to start; signed by a different key refuses to start; an unsigned manifest is accepted with a key configured; no key means nothing is checked (even an altered signed manifest is accepted, and the gate says so); the default key is used when no --pubkey is given; the default key refuses an altered manifest; an explicit --pubkey beats the default key; a configured key that cannot be loaded stops the gate (three cases: missing file, not a key, bad default key); policy-proxy refuses --pubkey. The existing signed-v0.3 gate test now documents that it is the no-key case.
The golden key and fingerprint constants in the new tests are the ones tests/signing.rs already uses (RFC 8032 section 7.1 test 1); I confirmed the fingerprint against the signed golden's own `signature.public_key_fingerprint` before relying on it.

MUTATION CHECKS (each applied by hand, run, reverted, rg residue scan clean afterward)
M1 signature check disabled: 3 tests fail (altered after signing, different key, default key + altered).
M2 a signature required once a key is configured: 1 test fails (a_configured_key_never_makes_a_signature_required).
M3 explicit --pubkey ignored in favour of the default: 6 fail, including an_explicit_pubkey_wins_over_the_default_key (the others fail because with HOME removed there is then no key at all).
M4 an unloadable configured key silently skipped: 1 fails (a_configured_key_that_cannot_be_loaded_stops_the_gate).
M5 the default key never consulted: 3 fail (default key used, default key refuses altered manifest, and the bad-default-key case).
M6 --pubkey accepted in policy-proxy mode: 1 fails (policy_proxy_refuses_pubkey_at_startup).
Not mutation-checked: the health `signature_key` value (asserted in 6 tests: the updated health test plus 5 new ones) and the two startup stderr lines (asserted in 2 tests); I did not mutate either.

My reading is that the rule is a keyword heuristic that started matching once the file mentions signatures; I did not change code to dodge it. ubs lists only 3 of the 7 sites, so "none of the 7 compares secret material" rests on my own listing of the file's comparisons, not on ubs.

comments.author: IndigoOriole
comments.text:
IndigoOriole, al-33c C5 (prev_hash-chained witness entries): estimate and design, posted BEFORE coding as the orchestrator asked. Orchestrator reorder acknowledged: al-33c C5 first, then al-b16, al-331, the rest of al-3pz and al-28e, al-210 last. I had started al-210 D-a groundwork; it was read-only (no edits, no reservations held, nothing to undo), and I have stopped it.

THIS CHANGES MY EARLIER "NOT CHEAP" ASSESSMENT ONLY PARTLY. What I got right: appends are one lock-free O_APPEND write, so a chain needs a lock. What I could not answer then and have now checked:
- The witness.v0 contract is not airlock-local, but the spine rules anticipate this. cmdrvl-context GOLDEN_RULES R-016: "If a chain field is ever present, treat it only as a local tamper hint, not as a substitute for lock or pack." R-017: witness write failures warn on stderr and never change the exit code. R-015: "Extra fields are permitted; missing required fields are a protocol violation."
- Other tools' ledger code that I read (hash/src/witness/ledger.rs) reads existing lines as serde_json::Value and ignores unknown members, and appends lock-free. No spine tool has a chain field today, so there is no name to collide with. I did NOT read pack, vacuum, fingerprint or lock readers beyond grepping them for deny_unknown_fields (none found).
- OBSERVATION, not part of C5 and not fixed: airlock's witness lines do not have the field names that the rvl and lock witness.v0 schema files require. The schemas (rvl/docs/witness.v0.schema.json, lock/schemas/witness-v0.schema.json) require id, tool, version, binary_hash, inputs, params, outcome, exit_code, output_hash, ts, with additionalProperties false; airlock writes witness_version, command, timestamp, stdout_hash, stdout_bytes. By R-015 that may already be a protocol violation, and it means "extra fields are permitted" is the spine rule while the schema files say otherwise. I compared field names only; I ran no other tool's validator on an airlock line. That needs an owner decision and is a separate bead if wanted (P0/P1 only this session, so I have not filed one).

DESIGN (my defaults; each can be reversed)
1. New optional member `prev_hash` on airlock's record: blake3 of the exact bytes of the previous AIRLOCK line (canonical JSON, no trailing newline). "Previous airlock line" = the last line in the ledger whose JSON `tool` is "airlock"; other tools' interleaved lines are skipped, because they do not honour any chain. The first airlock entry in an empty history carries the all-zero genesis hash. The first chained entry after legacy entries links to the last legacy airlock line, so existing history is committed to from then on.
2. Atomic read-last-then-append under an exclusive advisory lock on the ledger file, with a bounded wait (try_lock polling for about 2 seconds). If the lock cannot be taken, or the filesystem does not support it, the entry is appended UNCHAINED (no prev_hash) with a stderr warning, so a witness problem never changes the exit code (R-017) and the next entry links over it. The lock only serializes airlock processes and the gate's threads; other tools still do not take it.
3. A torn last line (no trailing newline after a crash) is terminated with a newline before the new entry rather than glued onto.
4. `airlock witness verify [--json] [--expect-head HASH]`: walks the airlock entries and checks each link; reports entries, chained, unchained, head hash, and breaks with line numbers and reasons (prev mismatch, first entry claims a predecessor, i.e. the head of the ledger was cut). Exit 0 when the chain holds, a distinct non-zero when it is broken. `--expect-head` fails if the current head differs from a hash the operator recorded elsewhere; that is the only defence against truncation of the tail (below).
5. Not doing: signing entries with the Ed25519 key. The key sits in the same user's home as the ledger, so it would not stop a same-user rewrite, and it would make a witness append depend on key access. Say so if you want it anyway.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT PROVE (will be in the README, per R-016 it is a hint)
- Detects: editing, deleting, inserting or reordering an airlock entry that is followed by a later airlock entry, and cutting entries off the head of the ledger.
- Does NOT detect: removing the last entries (the tail), or a full rewrite of the file by someone who can write it (they can recompute every hash). `--expect-head` with a head recorded off the ledger is the only mitigation I am adding.
- Entries written by other tools are neither covered nor checked.

ESTIMATE

Revision: main = master = 6fe78dd (pushed, fast-forward from b769c91). Shared tree pulled to 6fe78dd.
Commits:
- 24470de witness: chain airlock entries with prev_hash, written under a ledger lock (C5a)
- 10676cf tests: strict-manifest gate test waits for the gate's witness records
- f12be38 witness: airlock witness verify checks the prev_hash chain (C5b)
- 6fe78dd docs: README documents the witness chain and its limits; fix a stale exit-code row (C5c)
(Earlier for this bead: f88fa79 gate verifies manifest signatures when signed and a key is configured.)

CORRECTION to my own commit message: 24470de says "11 new unit tests". There are 13 new unit tests in src/witness/mod.rs plus 4 integration tests in tests/witness_chain.rs.

WHAT IT DOES
- Every airlock record (assemble, verify, gate) gets prev_hash = blake3:<hex> of the exact bytes (no newline) of the previous AIRLOCK line, or blake3: + 64 zeros for the first. Other tools' lines are skipped, not linked. An existing pre-chain ledger is extended: the first chained record links to the last older airlock line.
- Appends take an exclusive advisory lock on the ledger (std File::try_lock, polled every 10 ms for up to 2 s). If the lock cannot be taken the record is still appended WITHOUT prev_hash and a warning goes to stderr; exit codes never change (spine R-017). A torn last line gets a newline before the new record.
- `airlock witness verify [--expect-head HASH] [--json]`: exit 0 chain holds / no airlock records / no ledger; exit 1 CHAIN_BROKEN (PREV_HASH_MISMATCH, FIRST_ENTRY_HAS_PREDECESSOR, PREV_HASH_MALFORMED) or HEAD_MISMATCH; exit 2 refusal (unreadable ledger, malformed --expect-head). A break is reported on the record AFTER the one that changed. A record without prev_hash after the chain began is a warning, not a break. This is the first use of exit 1 among the witness commands.
- MSRV 1.88 -> 1.89 (Cargo.toml rust-version, AGENTS.md) because File::try_lock is stable in 1.89 and clippy incompatible_msrv would otherwise fail. CI uses stable; anyone building on 1.88 now cannot.

VERIFICATION AT THE EXACT REVISION
- Clean export of 6fe78dd (git archive HEAD into a fresh directory, so only committed files): cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, ast-grep scan, cargo test --locked, cargo build --locked --release: all rc=0. cargo test: 559 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (the ignored test was already ignored).
- GitHub CI run 45661134534 on 6fe78dd: success, all steps including Spine static rules.
- New tests: tests/witness_verify.rs 19 integration tests on ledgers written by real `airlock verify` runs, expected hashes computed by the test file itself (not by the code under test): edit, delete, insert, swap, head cut, malformed prev_hash, legacy extension, other tools' lines, empty/missing/unreadable ledger, malformed --expect-head, text output. 9 unit tests in src/witness/chain.rs, 1 CLI parse test. tests/witness_chain.rs: 3 waves x 8 concurrent real `airlock verify` processes produce one unbroken chain.
- Mutation checks, applied by hand, run, reverted (residue scan clean): C5b 11 mutations (never report a mismatch; never report a first-entry predecessor; head always None; any tool's line counted as airlock; HEAD_MISMATCH never reported; exit code always 0; warn on entries before the chain began; non-string prev_hash not a break; text report loses the reason name; --expect-head length unchecked; uppercase hex accepted). All 11 failed at least one test. Two (first-entry predecessor, warning before chain start) were first caught by only one integration test, so I added unit tests and re-checked both. C5a: 7 mutations were caught in the earlier session; I did not re-run those in this pass.

AN ERROR I MADE AND WHAT I FOUND
I committed 24470de after running only the witness lib tests, witness_chain and clippy, not the full suite. The clean export then failed strict_manifest_mode_forwards_only_a_preverified_canonical_request_hash. My first reading was that the new prev_hash field broke an assertion. That was wrong: the panic message prints the whole ledger, which now contains prev_hash, but the assertion is unrelated to it. The real cause is a race in the test: it reads the witness ledger right after its last response and has already dropped (killed) the gate, and the gate responds first and writes the receipt and witness record after. Measured, 80 runs of that one test, 16 in parallel: f88fa79 (before any chain code) 46 failed / 34 passed; 24470de 53 / 27; with the fix 10676cf, two batches of 80 = 160 passed, 0 failed. Run one at a time it passed 20 of 20, which is why earlier full-suite runs were green. So the race predates C5 and the chain did not cause it. 10676cf changes no assertion: the test now waits (up to 10 s) for three complete witness records before dropping the gate.

WHAT THE CHAIN DOES NOT DO (documented in README and operator.json; two tests pin the first two)
- Does not detect entries removed from the END of the ledger, nor a ledger rewritten whole by someone who recomputes every hash. Only --expect-head with a head kept off the ledger's writers' reach helps. It is a local tamper hint, spine R-016, not a proof.
- No per-entry signature. Covers airlock records only: another tool's lines are neither linked nor protected.
- Trimming old records off the front of a ledger is reported as a break (FIRST_ENTRY_HAS_PREDECESSOR); moving the whole file away starts a new chain.
- The lock is advisory and only orders airlock's own appends; other tools append without it.

NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED
- Everything above is my own runs. No second party re-executed it; the mutation checks and counts are mine.
- Tested on this machine (macOS) only. File::try_lock behaviour on other OSes or on network filesystems was not tested. Concurrency was tested at 8 threads x 40 appends and 3 waves x 8 processes.
- I did not run any other spine tool's witness validator. Observation only, from comparing field names: airlock's witness record uses witness_version, command, timestamp, stdout_hash, stdout_bytes, whereas the rvl and lock witness.v0 schemas use id, version, binary_hash, output_hash, ts with additionalProperties:false. Spine R-015 permits extra fields, which is why prev_hash is allowed, but this suggests the ledger lines may not be uniform across tools. Not touched by C5 and not fixed.
- I did not re-audit the rest of this bead's DESIGN/TESTS list in this pass. The two items I was asked to finish are the gate signature ruling (f88fa79) and C5.

DOC DRIFT FOUND
- README exit-code table said `witness query|last|count` with no matching records exits 1. Run against an empty and a missing ledger, all three exit 0 (operator.json already said so). README fixed in 6fe78dd.
- NOT fixed: docs/airlock_plan.md (around line 1108) still says a query with no matches exits 1. That is the spec; the shipped behaviour follows the spine contract. Left for the spec owner.

NEXT
Waiting on the orchestrator or a verifier to close al-33c; then al-b16 per the reorder (al-b16, al-331, rest of al-3pz and al-28e, al-210 last). I will not remove the al-3pz dependency on al-210/al-b16.

title: Phase A: detector packs in policy (secrets, PII, tabular dumps, blobs, paths)
description:
Parent: Airlock v1 epic. Depends on PA1 (findings plumbing).

PROBLEM: forbidden_patterns are filing-specific. A generic 'private data' story needs generic detectors so the tool is useful outside the BDC tournament.

DESIGN: policy YAML gains 'detectors: [secrets, pii, tabular, blobs, paths]' (all opt-in; tournament_baseline enables none to keep golden fixtures stable). Built-in packs in src/scanner/detectors/: secrets (AWS AKIA/ASIA keys, 'BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY', JWT shape, GitHub ghp_/github_pat_, Slack xox, generic 'api_key'/'secret' key names with high-entropy values), pii (US SSN with separators, card numbers passing Luhn, email, E.164/US phone, IBAN), tabular (>= N lines with the same delimiter count, N configurable default 5), blobs (base64 runs >= 512 chars, data: URIs), paths (absolute filesystem paths, ~/ paths, file:// URIs). Deterministic regex only; no ML. Each hit -> finding class DETECTED_SENSITIVE with detector id and JSON path, value NEVER echoed into the manifest (hash the matched span). Claim impact: any DETECTED_SENSITIVE hit -> BOUNDARY_FAILED, unless policy lists the detector under 'detectors_warn_only'.

TESTS: unit tests per detector with positives/negatives; false-positive corpus from fixtures (no hits on clean telemetry); the PII-append repro now fails on both REQUEST_UNBOUND and DETECTED_SENSITIVE; explain --json lists detector hits.

AMBITION ROUND ADDITIONS (2026-09-02): implement the packs in a workspace crate crates/boundary-detectors (published to crates.io as boundary-detectors, pinned by veil for broker output scanning and content sniffing - veil beads bd-27o and the sniff bead). API: fn scan(bytes, &PackSet) -> Vec<Hit {detector, byte_range, span_hash}>; never returns the matched text. Literal packs via aho-corasick; shapes via regex; Luhn for cards; Shannon entropy >= 3.5 bits/char over 20+ char tokens for generic secrets; tabular = N+ lines with equal delimiter counts; blobs = base64 runs >= 512 chars or data: URIs; paths = absolute/~/file:// . Per-detector thresholds. Fuzz target (cargo-fuzz) for panics on arbitrary bytes.
notes:
2026-11-24 review notes:
- Consume the shared `boundary-detectors` crate (shared with `veil` bd-35u / bd-27o) rather than duplicating regex/Aho-Corasick packs inside `airlock`.
- Include bounded recursive base64/hex decode-and-rescan so encoded CSVs/secrets/PII cannot slip past text detectors.
- Expose the shared one-way shingle Bloom matcher (`PROTECTED_CORPUS_MATCH`) for `airlock gate --protected-bloom`.
2026-11-25 Crate Live: public `github.com/cmdrvl/boundary-detectors` v0.1.0 is created and CI-green (fmt + clippy -D warnings + 13 tests). Consume it via `boundary-detectors = { git = "https://github.com/cmdrvl/boundary-detectors", rev = "0d4dd36fc07836dc67becf0647322c5ddd7dc6e8" }` instead of duplicating detector packs locally.
